reading.body:
Squire Patton Boggs filed 34 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI, with Tata Consultancy Services alone accounting for 11 of the 26 client filings listed.

The client list is the substance here. It runs from an Indian IT services giant to a staffing trade association to Vertiv, which makes data center power and cooling equipment. That spread is what AI lobbying looks like when it is about deployment rather than model research: the firms that build, staff, and power the systems are the ones registering to talk about it.

The lobbyist counts show a shallow bench rather than a deep one. David Schnittger appears on 16 AI filings, and four other lobbyists appear on 9 or more. Most of the 26 named lobbyists appear on 1 to 5. A handful of people carry the AI portfolio at this firm, which means the firm's AI work is concentrated in a few relationships rather than distributed across the practice.

What the data does not say is what any of these clients argued. A filing reports that a firm lobbied on an issue, not the position taken, so the direction of the advocacy is invisible here. The data also does not identify which AI bills were named, and it covers one firm only, so it cannot show whether this client mix is typical of AI lobbying overall.
